question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Any termination performed after the first trimester of pregnancy
options.B: A procedure carried out by unskilled persons or in environments below minimal medical standards
options.C: Any spontaneous miscarriage that occurs without medical supervision
options.D: A legal termination performed in a tertiary teaching hospital

explanation: An unsafe abortion is formally defined as a procedure for terminating an unintended pregnancy carried out either by persons lacking necessary skills or in environments lacking minimal medical standards. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following is a primary driver of unsafe abortion practices in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal access to free contraceptive services
options.B: Restrictive legal frameworks and societal stigma
options.C: An abundance of trained medical personnel in rural areas
options.D: Excessive availability of safe clinical facilities

explanation: Restrictive legal frameworks, societal stigma, poverty, and limited access to modern contraceptives drive women toward clandestine, unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: What is the primary mechanism leading to hemorrhage in incomplete unsafe abortions?

options.A: Spontaneous rupture of the renal arteries
options.B: Inability of the uterus to contract effectively due to retained products of conception
options.C: Direct chemical toxicity from herbal douches

explanation: Retained products of conception prevent the uterus from contracting effectively (uterine atony), leading to continuous and severe hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: How do infectious pathogens typically enter the reproductive tract during an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Through hematogenous spread from upper respiratory infections
options.B: As ascending polymicrobial flora from the lower genital tract introduced by unsterile instruments

explanation: Infectious pathogens are usually ascending polymicrobial flora from the lower genital tract introduced by unsterile instruments colonizing necrotic tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: Which of the following represents an acute complication of an unsafe abortion?
explanation: Hypovolemic shock and visceral perforation are acute, life-threatening complications that manifest immediately or within days of an unsafe abortion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: What is a common long-term reproductive consequence of post-abortion pelvic infections?
explanation: Chronic infections and PID lead to scarring and tubal occlusion, which directly cause secondary infertility and higher risks of ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which demographic group is disproportionately affected by unsafe abortion in Nigeria due to social stigma?

options.A: Multiparous older women in urban areas
options.B: Adolescents, young women, and unmarried individuals

explanation: Adolescents, young women, and unmarried individuals face high rates due to cultural stigma surrounding premarital sex and barriers to reproductive services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: How do poverty and rural residency contribute to the incidence of unsafe abortions?

options.A: By providing surplus access to safe clinical surgical centers
options.B: By forcing women to rely on cheap, clandestine, and unqualified practitioners due to lack of funds and transport
options.C: By eliminating the biological risk of unwanted pregnancies
options.D: By guaranteeing universal health insurance coverage

explanation: Financial hardship and lack of transport prevent women from accessing safe care, driving them toward unqualified practitioners and unsafe methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: What is the immediate priority during the initial nursing triage of a patient with suspected unsafe abortion complications?

options.B: Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation (ABCs) for shock
options.D: Discharging the patient with oral antibiotics

explanation: Initial triage must always prioritize the ABCs to identify and treat life-threatening conditions such as hemorrhagic or septic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: Which diagnostic imaging modality is most valuable for confirming retained products of conception?
explanation: Pelvic ultrasonography is invaluable for visualizing retained products of conception, assessing endometrial thickness, and detecting free peritoneal fluid. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is the appropriate initial IV fluid resuscitation approach for a patient in hypovolemic shock from abortion-related hemorrhage?

options.A: Restricting fluids to prevent pulmonary edema
options.B: Administering large-bore IV access and infusing isotonic crystalloids rapidly

explanation: Large-bore IV access and rapid infusion of isotonic crystalloids are essential first steps to restore intravascular volume in hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: Why is prompt administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics critical in patients with suspected septic abortion?

options.B: To combat ascending polymicrobial infections and prevent septic shock

explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics combat ascending polymicrobial pathogens found in necrotic uterine tissue, halting progression to severe sepsis and septic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: When can a woman typically return to fertility following an abortion, making post-abortion contraception vital?

options.A: After a mandatory six-month waiting period
options.C: Only after full surgical healing of the cervix in one year
options.D: Fertility does not return until the following year

explanation: A woman can return to fertility within weeks of an abortion, making immediate pre-discharge contraceptive counseling and provision essential to prevent rapid repeat pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: Which of the following is a primary objective of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Punishing the patient for breaking legal regulations
options.B: Treating acute complications, offering contraception, and providing holistic counseling
options.C: Ensuring permanent sterilization for all patients
options.D: Mandating reporting to law enforcement agencies

explanation: PAC is a holistic model focused on treating complications, providing contraceptive counseling, addressing emotional needs, and preventing future unintended pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: What is an effective preventative nursing strategy to reduce the incidence of unsafe abortion in communities?

options.B: Participating in community sex education and providing youth-friendly family planning services
options.C: Enforcing mandatory detention for women seeking abortions
options.D: Restricting access to basic healthcare clinics

explanation: Community sex education and youth-friendly family planning services empower individuals to prevent unintended pregnancies, reducing reliance on unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h8)

question: How can clinical nurses contribute to institutional improvements in post-abortion and reproductive care?

options.A: By refusing to treat patients who have undergone induced abortions
options.B: By challenging provider bias and advocating for training in safe evacuation techniques like MVA
options.C: By ignoring psychological trauma to save time
options.D: By limiting contraceptive counseling to older married women

explanation: Challenging provider bias ensures respectful, non-discriminatory care, while advocating for MVA training improves clinical safety and efficiency. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h8)
